builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification
summary: Prefill1 replaces full generative verification output (quote-and-classify error lists) with prefilled fixed syntax tokens plus a single generated branch token, stopping decoding at the empty-list versus first-error decision point. It requires a frozen 2B verifier with a rigid structured output schema and known fixed token prefix, adding prompt-construction logic but no training; quality is near-identical (F1 83.43 vs 83.41) yet the paper reports small decision changes, and 6.74-26.73% savings under compiled execution rather than the headline 84.84%. It fails when downstream consumers need error localization or quoted spans, when the output schema or instruction changes (invalidating the prefilled prefix), or when the early branch decision diverges from what full decoding would have produced.
rationale: The technique is a cheap, training-free decoding trick on a frozen small verifier, but its benefit depends on having a fixed-output-schema verification workload and it introduces small decision changes, so it should be validated on the reader's own tasks before production use.

claims.statement: Prefill1 replaces full generative verification output (quote-and-classify error lists) with prefilled fixed syntax tokens plus a single generated branch token, stopping decoding at the empty-list versus first-error decision point. It requires a frozen 2B verifier with a rigid structured output schema and known fixed token prefix, adding prompt-construction logic but no training; quality is near-identical (F1 83.43 vs 83.41) yet the paper reports small decision changes, and 6.74-26.73% savings under compiled execution rather than the headline 84.84%. It fails when downstream consumers need error localization or quoted spans, when the output schema or instruction changes (invalidating the prefilled prefix), or when the early branch decision diverges from what full decoding would have produced.

Prefill1 reduces eager resident service by 84.84% relative to full generation (released-reference F1 83.43 vs 83.41) and by 31.98% over Native8 on 2,015 code-agent test responses; extra saving of 6.74-26.73% under default compiled execution.
